checks: Source digest matches the original note. Section 2, (5), supplies the same product body, affine q_p, strict cover, cap volume, normalized integral and limiting closed mass. The extra nonattainment sentence in the draft proof is valid in its stated smaller budget interval.
On the binary sites q_p equals Hamming distance. For z≠p, λ_j-t-Aq_p≤1-t-A<0. At z=p some coordinate is at least 1/(d+1)>t, so the corresponding cap contains the point strictly.

The threshold-s region is obtained by dilating the simplex about vertex j by 1-s; its volume is v(1-s)^d. The layer integral from t to 1 gives v(1-t)^(d+1)/(d+1), including d=1. The n base coefficients each have magnitude A, so the square of the full normal norm is nA²+|∇λ_j|².

As t tends to 1/(d+1) from below, the mass ratio tends down to 2^(-n)γ_d. Any strict gap above that ratio allows one fixed t and all A>1. At fixed t each normalized hinge is O(A^(-1)), while the normalized affine margin tends to -q_p/√n. Its nonnegative set has exactly the binary fiber p and closed mass v.

When τM<v a vertical cap meeting the source is infeasible. A feasible cover must place an inball center in a nonvertical cap; the nonzero continuous component yields positive hinge on part of the inball. This verifies the proof's additional zero-infimum nonattainment observation.

overlap.comparison: The exposed-fiber tilt construction already isolates a chosen binary fiber while preserving its own cap, and the exact cube–simplex depth ratio is the same γ_d 2^(-n). That theorem does not address ambient-unit hinge, the fixed strict cover family, or the positive mass of its vertical closed limit.
The sharpness proof uses the canonical barycentric cover and homothetic cap volume at t=1/(d+1) in one simplex. It does not use a diverging base tilt or calculate the normalized mixed-source hinge.

Its interval-cylinder example gives near-vertical balanced caps through one mark with fixed mass. It does not give a fixed-count strict cover with vanishing total hinge or the cube–simplex construction.

readability: The normalized affine margins converge on the source and pointwise in the ambient space. The closed limit here means the cap of the limiting affine margin, which includes the full boundary fiber.
